messages:
maya: Heads up — after the cni rollout to cilium v1.22 in west3 we're seeing sporadic packet loss for GPU training pods. Several jobs hit gRPC timeouts and retries.

deploy-bot: cilium/v1.22 rolled to cluster west3 at 2026-03-18T11:02:00Z by infra-ci (canary -> 80% -> 100%).

samir: confirming, noticed a spike in retransmits on node gpu-3a-host-07 around 11:05. tcp_retrans_out and ifconfig errors.

jules: can you paste the node-level counters? I want to check GSO/GRO and TSO stats.

samir: quick grab from gpu-3a-host-07: 
```
ethtool -k eth0 | grep -i generic
rx-checksumming: on
tx-checksumming: on
scatter-gather: on
tcp-segmentation-offload: on
generic-segmentation-offload: on
generic-receive-offload: on
```
and `dmesg` has a bunch of `cilium bpf: XDP_DROP` entries around the same timeframe.

maya: job-level symptoms — increased p99 latency on RPCs; one training job retried, lost ~30% throughput. This impacts our reserved GPU capacity utilisation and may push some customers to delay runs — potential cost/ops hit if we need to reprovision.

lars: I see a pattern in perf data: east-west flows (pod->pod on same host) okay, but cross-node east-west has bursts of loss under high packet rate (grpc blobs). Might be path MTU/GSO coalescing issue with the new BPF policies.

jules: can you show `ip route` + `ip link` mtu on those hosts? also any changes in CNI default mtu?

samir: host config snippets: 
```
ip link show dev eth0
3: eth0: mtu 1500 qdisc fq_codel state UP mode DEFAULT group default qlen 1000
```
Cilium config in the rollout: `tunnel: geneve`, `mtu: 1450` (we set to 1450 in config map to account for overlay).

maya: but kernel shows 1500 and cilium overlay 1450 — mismatch maybe when GSO merges segments across overlay we end up with oversized packets and XDP rejects?

jules: I'm seeing a known regression note in Cilium 1.22 about GSO handling with Geneve on some NIC drivers — can cause fragmented large segments to be dropped when HW offload flags are present.

lars: quick experiment: disable GRO/GSO on node and rerun a failing job.

samir: did `sudo ethtool -K eth0 gso off gro off tso off` on gpu-3a-host-07 and restarted a small synthetic load (iperf3 UDP stream + grpc echo). Observed that retransmits drop to baseline and job completes without timeouts.

maya: that suggests offload interaction. But disabling offloads cluster-wide isn't great for throughput/cost — will increase CPU per-token and could push us over committed GPU/host capacity.

jules: short term: roll back cilium to v1.21 in west3? That would revert the change and restore offload-friendly path. Long term: upstream patch or set Cilium options to disable problematic offload features selectively.

oncall-bot: incident created: #INC-2026-0318-02 — west3 cni regression affecting GPU cross-node traffic. Priority: P2.

lars: pros/cons — rollback now buys latency back but means running older CNI across other clusters; rollback window is 30m. Patch route requires QA and vendor signoff which could be days.

maya: business impact note: a couple of queued enterprise jobs might miss SLAs if we wait. If rollback is quick we avoid scaling extra reserved capacity; if not, we should consider temporarily draining noisy nodes or shifting jobs to east1 to avoid SLA misses (but migration costs $$$).

samir: I can start a rollback canary to a subset of nodes (5 nodes) in west3 now and watch the p95/p99.

jules: do it, and also patch a host-level workaround: set `bpf-forwarding` config to avoid GSO touching encapsulation (there's a cilium option `no-gso-encap` in some builds) — but that option is only in the version with the upstream fix.

maya: rollback started at 11:25. deploy-bot will post completion.

deploy-bot: rollback to cilium/v1.21 initiated for west3 canary group at 2026-03-18T11:25:00Z.

samir: after rolling 5 nodes back, retransmits returned to baseline and training job resumed. p99 latencies dropped from ~1.6s to ~230ms.

lars: confirm: `ethtool -k` output unchanged but drop counters cleared after rollback.

jules: next steps: 1) pin west3 to v1.21 until upstream patch lands; 2) open ticket with Cilium with captures (pcap+kern logs); 3) run controlled perf tests with large-GSO flows to verify.

maya: agreed. I'll update customer-facing status and ops runbook (how to rollback cni and the mitigation of draining noisy nodes).

oncall-bot: incident updated: rollback mitigated impact. Monitoring will continue for next 4 hours.

samir: leaving a note: if we have to keep v1.21 longer, we should schedule a canary in a staging cluster and test offload-heavy workloads with geneve to avoid surprise.

jules: also write a small reproducer (grpc blob generator) so infra QA can verify future fixes. I'll push a repo with scripts.

maya: thanks all. I'll follow up with a postmortem draft in #postmortems and mark impacted customer jobs in billing so we can assess cost exposure. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: reminder — file an upstream bug and attach the `cilium-bpf.log` and `pcap` captured during the incident.

maya: noted. I'll attach logs to the incident and ping @cilium-team.
